summary: Anderson County steel tower built around 1938 by the SC Forestry Commission; sold to a private owner, who was renovating it as of 2017.

access.note: Sold to a private owner in 1990 per the register; the owner was renovating it as of 2017; no public access described in the sources read

events.note: Built circa 1938 by the SC Forestry Commission, per the register
Sold to a private owner, which the register places after the abandonment of the state's tower system
Owner renovating the tower as of 2017, per the register
Registered 23 August 2017; nominated by Ted Brown

evidence.supports: 75-foot Bethlehem Steel tower built circa 1938 by SCFC
evidence.quote: This 75-foot Bethlehem Steel fire tower was built circa 1938 by the South Carolina Forestry Commission.

evidence.supports: sold to a private owner in 1990 after abandonment of the system
evidence.quote: It was sold to a private owner in 1990 after the abandonment of South Carolina's fire tower system.

evidence.supports: renovation under way by new owner as of 2017
evidence.quote: As of 2017, the tower is being renovated by its new owner.

evidence.supports: administered by Ted D. Brown (basis for agency correction)
first SCFC tower erected August 1930 near Camden
evidence.quote: The first Forestry Commission fire tower was erected in August, 1930 near Camden.
The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

corrections.why: The register's 'Administered by' field names the private owner, not an agency. The Forestry Commission built the tower; the owner has held it since 1990 after a sale.

notes_for_editor: Thin sourcing: only the register and the SCFC history page were readable. Two dates conflict and are unresolved: the register puts the 1990 private sale 'after the abandonment' of the state system, but SCFC says it closed the system on 1 October 1993. Unread sources: a Facebook group post by Ted Brown says the tower was built in 1938/1939 (fetch returned title only, so not used); a Waymarking page calls it the summit of the county's highest point (fetch returned title only, not used). Do not confuse this with the Little Mountain in Newberry County, which has a Wikipedia article. Height 75 ft converted to 22.9 m from the register.
